market_holds: Event-implied move 7.23% (front-expiry straddle 7.42%, ATM spread 43% of mid so indicative only), 25d skew +5.4 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.87 (sealed baseline, 18:08 UTC). Median prior reaction 6.97% over 7 prints, last two +13.58% (Jul, Q4 guide with Meta deal) and -10.41% (Apr, weak Q3 guide). Run-in: $64.67 on 11-10 to $59.65 intraday 11-17 (-7.8%) against QQQ -2.9%, SPY -2.4%, IDCC -7.4% (Yahoo daily bars); the last three sessions -7.6% vs QQQ -4.8%, so mostly tape and licensing-peer selling, plus a Rosenblatt target cut 85->80 on 11-16 (stockanalysis). Before that the stock had run +14.6% since the July print (Earnings Whispers preview 11-10). Q4 consensus ~$368M revenue / $1.19 EPS (EW, 11-10), about $9M below the $377M guide midpoint; whisper $1.26. FY27 consensus revenue $1.47B (+3.3%) and EPS $4.58 (+6%) (stockanalysis, 4 analysts, read 11-17). Bearish sentiment 55.7% vs 37.8% a quarter ago (EW). The line it trades on: the next-quarter and initial FY27 guide, with the memory-cost hit to mobile/PC units against VDP (Meta), auto and wearables.
view: Q4 FY26 itself should land at or above the low-set consensus: management built Meta's large VDP deal (signed early in Q4) and back-end-loaded mobile minimum volume commitments into a guide whose midpoint consensus sits below, and the CFO said memory effects were already factored in. The September-quarter collapse in units (smartphones -22% y/y per IDC, PCs -20%/-22% per IDC/Gartner, published Oct 8-15) looks bad but is roughly what IDC's May forecast of -13.9% for calendar 2026 already implied for the second half, so it is not obviously a surprise against the July guide. The print will turn on the initial FY27 and Q1 guide. There the evidence cuts both ways: PC is 10-12% of licensing and mobile is the most memory-exposed market, and Oct-Dec 2026 units will compare against a strong Oct-Dec 2025, which argues for a cautious Q1 (Dolby's Q1 FY26 guide also landed below consensus a year ago); against that, MVCs cushion mobile, Meta and the VDP pool should now recur, auto is the fastest-growing market, and consensus at +3.3% FY27 revenue is not demanding. Last year's initial FY guide ($1.39-1.44B) brought a near-flat reaction. The stock already gave back about half of its post-July gain in a week, mostly with the tape and with IDCC, which sold off despite beating and raising. I cannot show that either side of the guide line is more likely than the price assumes, so there is no recommendation; a slight lean down for guide-conservatism risk on Q1.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the initial FY27/Q1 guide. The memory-driven unit decline is public, dated and flagged by management, while the offsets (Meta/VDP recurrence, MVCs, auto) are also known. Consensus FY27 at +3.3% is modest, and the stock has already fallen ~8% into the print with the tape. I find no dated evidence that puts one side of the guide more likely than the price assumes.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q1 FY27 revenue guide well below the roughly $345M year-ago level, or an FY27 midpoint under ~$1.43B, would make a down move likely. An FY27 midpoint at or above $1.47B with Meta described as recurring would make an up move likely from a sold-off price.

self_critique: The case for a down call: Oct-Dec 2026 mobile and PC units compare against a strong prior year after a ~20% collapse, and Dolby has a record of guiding Q1 below consensus, so the next-quarter guide (the line the last reactions turned on) could disappoint as it did in April (-10%). The case for an up call: Q4 should beat a consensus set below the guide midpoint, Meta's VDP revenue should recur, and the stock has already fallen ~8% with the tape. Both sides are plausible and I could not quantify either beyond public data the price has had for a month.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: comparing with IDCC (which sold off on a beat) showed the -8% was sector and tape, not company news. P7's push to estimate the unseen guide line was hard here: the inputs (unit data) are public and roughly offset by contract cushions, so there was no honest way to move far from 50.
